data.long_meaning: The name Jaivansh is derived from two Sanskrit roots: ‘Jaiv’ which means ‘living’ and ‘Ansh’ which means ‘descendant’. This name signifies the one who is the descendant of living beings, implying the strength and vitality of life. The name Jaivansh carries the meaning “Descendant of living beings” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jaivansh usually hope their child will grow to embody descendant of living beings and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: The Jaivansh dynasty was a lineage of Hindu rulers who ruled over the region of Mathura in the northern Indian subcontinent from the 7th to the 12th centuries CE. The name Jaivansh is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Jiva' (living being) and 'Vansh' (descendants). The dynasty is believed to have originated from the Yadavas, who were the kinsmen of Lord Krishna.

The Jaivansh rulers were initially vassals of the Pratihara kings, but later gained independence and ruled over Mathura as sovereign kings. They were known for their patronage of art, architecture, and literature. The most famous Jaivansh ruler was King Hemchandra, who is credited with the construction of the famous temple of Keshavraji in Mathura.
